summary: A complete batched serving engine for a synthetic transformer: a Core ConcurrentModel with mixed batches whose steps run every request's rows through one GEMM per weight, StateCache pages with prefix reuse, paged-attention kernels, batch-invariant arithmetic and a native engine library served concurrently by crit serve
implementation_scope: CUDA and C++ source: synthetic decoder layers (RMSNorm, fused QKV with split-half rotary embedding, grouped-query paged attention, SiLU MLP, LM head) with seeded weights; a BF16 tensor-core GEMM with a K split fixed per weight shape and device and an ordered split reduction; row-local norm, rotary, SiLU and argmax kernels; a ConcurrentModel with execute() over mixed decode and prompt rows, StateCache prefix attach and reuse reporting, page-reserving admission, reuse hints, host sampling through Core's Sampler and device greedy argmax; make_engine() for a Core Engine; a native engine library with concurrent_requests; a throughput-versus-concurrency tool; a host model of the step layout, split plan and admission. A real model's weights, tokenizer, layer arithmetic and faster kernels are engine supplied.

agent_guidance.use_when: An engine needs to serve several requests at once with shared steps, needs a working skeleton that combines Core's concurrent scheduler, the StateCache and paged attention, or a scheduler or kernel change must be measured under concurrency without a checkpoint
agent_guidance.avoid_when: The engine serves one request at a time, the model is not a dense softmax-attention decoder, or a production model's quality matters (the weights are random)
provides: One mixed step: decode rows first, then prompt chunks, every projection one GEMM over all rows so weights are read once per step

Batch invariance: row-local kernels, a GEMM K split fixed per weight and device, phase-chosen attention kernels with position-only results, lowest-id argmax; batched output equals serial output token for token
StateCache sequences per request with prefix attach in open(), reused_prompt_tokens on the first prompt step, commit and discard of rounds, retirement after synchronized steps
Admission that reserves a request's whole page need and scheduling hints with reusable tokens
Host sampling through Core's Sampler for temperature, top-k/p, min-p, penalties and bias, device argmax for plain greedy rows
A native engine library (CRIT_EXPORT_ENGINE, concurrent_requests) that crit_core.native.resident_engine serves as chat-concurrent-v1
A throughput-versus-concurrency tool reporting completion tokens over the wave's wall time
engine_supplies: The model's weights, layer arithmetic, tokenizer and chat template
Faster kernels (fused epilogues, quantized projections, CUDA graphs per batch shape) that keep the batch invariance rules
Device-memory sizing of the page pool and the batch bounds from the target context and concurrency
preserve: A row's arithmetic never depends on the other rows of its step or on prompt chunk boundaries
Keys and values written only at Round::kv slots before the attention that reads them; every round committed or discarded
Released pages retired only after the work that read them settled
Admission keeps every admitted request able to finish
The prefix identity names the weights and the KV representation
adapt: Model layers, normalization, positional encoding and weight formats
Asynchronous steps (BatchExecution) instead of a synchronized step, with retire() at the readiness point
Admission accounting that credits shared prefix pages, and memory preemption
GEMM tiles and split policy, sampling on the device

code_files.purpose: Model shape and the GEMM, norm, rotary, SiLU, conversion and argmax interfaces
Batch-invariant kernels: seeded weights, split-K tensor-core GEMM with ordered reduction, row-local kernels
The ConcurrentModel: mixed steps, StateCache with prefix reuse, paged attention, admission, sampling; make_engine()
Native engine library with concurrent requests, configured from JSON
Throughput against concurrency: completion tokens over each wave's wall time
Host model of the step layout, the GEMM split plan and admission

requires.hardware: CUDA C++20 on sm_80+ (BF16 mma.sync, ldmatrix, cp.async; paged-attention's requirements); builds checked for sm_80, sm_86, sm_89 and sm_120, runtime validation on sm_120 only; Python 3.11+ standard library for the reference
requires.model: Dense decoder-only softmax attention with grouped-query heads, head dimension 64, 128 or 256 and dimensions in multiples of 64 (synthetic weights)
requires.workload: Concurrent requests with mixed prompt and decode steps, prefix reuse and greedy or sampled decoding

contract.input: Token prompts, output limits and request options through Core's Engine or the native ABI; a JSON configuration naming the shape, page format and bounds
contract.output: Generated tokens with Core's request timing (reused_prompt_tokens included); per-step logits rows on the device
contract.ownership: Core's worker thread makes every model call; the model owns weights, pages, scratch and the StateCache; each step ends with the compute stream synchronized
contract.failure: Invalid shapes and configurations throw at construction; requests longer than the context or larger than the page pool are infeasible; CUDA errors throw and fail the engine through Core
contract.core_boundary: No Core change: ConcurrentModel, StateCache, Sampler, CudaBackend and the native engine ABI as published

dependencies: Python standard library for the reference

validation.host: The README example: the K split plan depends only on shape and device, a split dot product equals the plain one, a mixed step's row layout and logits rows, admission's page need
validation.native: GEMM against an FP64 host product (split and unsplit, stored and accumulated) and bitwise across row counts; norm, rotary, SiLU and argmax against host references (argmax equal to Core's greedy Sampler with ties); nine requests batched with other prompt chunking equal their serial runs token for token with BF16 and E4M3 pages, greedy and seeded sampling, with mixed steps of up to 9 requests and 48 reused prompt tokens reported for a repeated prompt; concurrent HTTP replies through crit serve equal solo replies
validation.performance: RTX 5090, synthetic model of 0.98 GB BF16 weights (hidden 2,048, 8 layers, 16/4 heads of 128, FFN 5,632, vocabulary 32,000), 128-token prompts and outputs: 535 completion tokens/s for one request, 2,347 for 4, 8,351 for 16, 16,627 for 32 and 28,958 for 64 concurrent requests, with 540 to 590 tokens/s per request; no claim for other devices or models
